page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-64-standardlssd is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the Storage Optimized machine family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 504.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

A defining characteristic of this configuration is its high-capacity integrated storage layer. The machine is provisioned with 15,032 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across four physical drive partitions. This direct-attached NVMe pool provides substantial local scratch space and high I/O throughput directly to the host instance, eliminating network-attached storage latency for primary data access. Standard networking is utilized without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

From an architectural perspective, the high density of dedicated cores, expansive memory array, and massive bundled NVMe capacity positions this instance for intensive I/O operations and low-latency storage workloads. The balance of 7.88 GB of RAM per core approaches memory-optimized ratios while providing exceptional local capacity per compute unit. However, because local NVMe disks are ephemeral, resilient architecture requires external replication or snapshot strategies. Appropriate workloads include large-scale transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching tiers requiring local persistent disk staging, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-64-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs and 504.0 GB of memory. It features an integrated high-capacity local storage tier consisting of 15,032 GB across four local NVMe SSDs, yielding low-latency input/output operations directly at the host level without hardware GPU acceleration. With a ratio of approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance bridges memory-intensive and storage-heavy resource profiles. The resource configuration delivers cost-efficient density for storage-bound architectures by pairing heavy computational capability directly with massive attached high-speed solid-state drives. It is particularly suited for high-transaction distributed databases, NoSQL stores, real-time telemetry processing, large-scale data warehousing nodes, and analytics engines that demand fast, direct disk access alongside extensive memory capacity.
